title: Banque Delubac & Cie says intrusion led to failed fraud attempt and a leak of some customers' data
date_note: Banque Delubac & Cie's press release of 23 November says it detected the intrusion on Friday 20 November.
summary: French bank Banque Delubac & Cie says it detected an intrusion in its information systems on 20 November, with an attempt at fraudulent financial transactions that failed. The bank says the intrusion led to a leak of data on part of its customers, with the extent still under investigation, and that it informed the ACPR and CNIL and filed a complaint. Suspended fund movements were restored on 23 November, it says.
plain: A French bank, Banque Delubac & Cie, says hackers got into its systems and tried to move money but failed. Some customers' data leaked; the bank is still working out how much.
exec: A bank intrusion stopped short of fraud but still leaked part of the customer data, with the extent still unknown.
action: Banque Delubac & Cie reminds customers, as Le Monde Informatique reports, that its teams never ask for access codes or passwords by SMS, email or phone; it also warned of fraudulent SMS posing as the bank.

sources.name: Banque Delubac & Cie press release (French), 23 Nov 2026

validation.note: Primary: the bank's own press release of 23 Nov on delubac.com (detection on 20 Nov, failed fraud attempt, leak of part of the customer data, ACPR and CNIL informed, complaint filed, services restored Monday morning). Le Monde Informatique (23 Nov) reports the same and the SMS warning posted on the bank's website; it says no link between that SMS campaign and the intrusion has been established. Neither gives a number of customers or the data types.
